summary: Outstanding refund reversals are never retried automatically (TKT-157 follow-up)
description:
Found by the TKT-157 adversarial review (finding F3). Recorded rather than fixed there, for the reasons in ADR-038 §7.

A refund whose money moved but whose tickets were not voided — access down, `ACCESS_URL` unset, or issuance not caught up (503) — is **visible** (`order_refunds.tickets_voided_at IS NULL`) and **retryable** (replay the same idempotency key). Nothing retries it. The reviewer's sharpest point: the caller receives an HTTP **200**, so there is no signal telling it to come back, and the outstanding obligation depends on someone noticing `tickets_voided:false`.

TKT-157's AC asked for *visible and retryable*, which is met. Automatic retry is a different requirement, and a second recovery state machine in commerce is a large cost to add on the strength of a review finding rather than a stated need — so it was deferred here, not dismissed. TKT-161 adds `capacity_returned_at` as a second outstanding obligation of the same shape, which is the natural moment to decide whether one runner should drive both.

Related in kind: **TKT-146** (no operator path to resolve or unpark a parked recovery order).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] An outstanding reversal is driven to completion without a human replaying the request, or there is an explicitly monitored, documented reconciler that is part of the deployment contract.
- [ ] Whatever drives it is idempotent against the downstream operations, which already are.
- [ ] A test drives a downstream outage and proves the obligation completes afterwards.
- [ ] Decide, and record, whether missing `ACCESS_URL` should become a readiness failure — ADR-038 §7 currently makes it a deliberate degradation.

Quality gates: `make check` green; contract tests; money untouched.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.

Traceability is a must, for money and tickets: money-relevant records land as immutable, hash-chained, signed journal entries from the first order (corrections = compensating entries; read models = projections), and every ticket/entitlement state change (issued, delivered, transferred, resold, exchanged, redeemed, reissued, invalidated) is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order.

governingAdrs.why: Every lifecycle event goes through store.appendLifecycle — the verifier asserts one-to-one coverage, so a direct INSERT into lifecycle_events reads as tampering and fails `access verify-lifecycle` in the gate. Canonical forms are pinned by golden literals; changing a byte is a canonical-version migration, not a test update. Also: name the adversary before writing 'tamper-evident'.

Inventory's claim transaction is the contention path. Giving capacity back must go through the same row-locked transaction discipline; a plain UPDATE outside it can drive confirmed_quantity negative or double-return under concurrency.
Capacity adjustments clamp rather than reject. Returning capacity must not let availability exceed the pool's capacity, and the clamp reasoning is the precedent for what to do when it would.

Corrections are COMPENSATING ENTRIES, never mutations. A refund/exchange appends a new signed fact; the original sale fact and its hash link are untouched. The payments journal has a DB trigger that raises on UPDATE/DELETE — any design that 'adjusts' a fact is rejected by the database, not by review.

If any domain event payload changes or a new one is published: bump on CONSUMER SEMANTICS, not parse compatibility, and consumers dispatch on `schema` BEFORE decoding `data`. A fixture built from the type under test cannot fail.

Fail closed. Responses are validated against the spec; an undeclared status code becomes a 500. Every new endpoint must declare every status it can answer, and a downstream answer commerce cannot validate aborts rather than degrades.

Contract-first. A new operation is written in the service's openapi.yaml first, then `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` are regenerated and COMMITTED before the gate runs — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.
Commerce and inventory ARE inside the smoke happy-path coverage gate. A new documented 2xx operation must be exercised through the running stack or the suite fails.

Migrations run out-of-band via each binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job. Add the SQL under the service's internal/store/migrations/ with the next number; the server path never migrates.

objective.note: A transient access outage currently leaves refunded tickets valid until a human replays the refund.

scope.note: IN: driving outstanding reversal obligations to completion. OUT: the money path, which is already durable and already recovered.

uncertainties.note: Runner vs outbox vs external reconciler is a Planning-time call. Best taken after TKT-161, when both obligations exist and one mechanism can cover both.

dependencies.note: Not blocked, but worth sequencing after TKT-161 so the design covers both obligations rather than being retrofitted.

first_slice.note: Drive the ticket-voiding obligation after a simulated access outage.

success.note: Demoable: stop access, refund, restart access, watch the reversal complete with no human action.

context_memo.note: Inherited from TKT-157; ADR-038 §7 records the rejected design and why.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ⚠️ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

Shapeable now, better after TKT-161. Two obligations of identical shape will exist then, and deciding the mechanism against one of them risks a design that has to be retrofitted for the second.

**Concerns:** (1) sequencing, above. (2) The `ACCESS_URL`-as-readiness question is a deployment-contract decision, not purely engineering.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — proceedable, but hold for TKT-161.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 — promoted to Ready (owner, 2026-08-17)

**Outstanding refund reversals are never retried automatically.**

Its deferral has now been *satisfied*, which is why it is promotable. `uncertainties`,
`dependencies` and `approach` were all deferred with one shared reason: *"best taken after TKT-161,
when both obligations exist and one mechanism can cover both."* **TKT-161 is Done.** The condition
the deferral named has been met, so the Planning-time call (runner vs outbox vs external
reconciler) can now be taken against both obligations rather than retrofitted to one.

**On `approach: deferred` and the money-path carve-out** — `shaping.md` says a deferred approach
does *not* pass when a ticket touches money. Called out rather than glossed: the exception does not
bite here, because what is deferred is a **mechanism choice among three known options**, not a
decision about who may spend or what a trust boundary is. The obligation is already visible
(`order_refunds.tickets_voided_at IS NULL`) and already retryable by replaying the idempotency key.
If Planning finds the choice is actually about authorization, that is a signal to stop and
re-shape.

**Verified before promoting, not assumed:** all eight DoR items are `met` or `deferred` with none
`open`, and every `blocked-by` link resolves to a **Done** ticket. Promoted as part of a sweep of
every fully-shaped Backlog ticket, on the owner's instruction.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — Ready → Planning

Running **gateless per `config.gates: autonomous`** (local tracker backend, `config.tracker: local`).
Gate 1 was taken by the owner on 2026-08-17; gates 2-4 are the agent's on this run.

**Selection reason.** Requested by name for an autonomous end-to-end run. Its Gate 1 promotion note
records that the deferral condition — *"best taken after TKT-161, when both obligations exist and one
mechanism can cover both"* — is now satisfied: **TKT-161 is Done**, and `order_refunds` carries both
`tickets_voided_at` and `capacity_returned_at`. Verified on the board, not assumed.

**Blockers.** Zero open. The only link is `found-in: TKT-157` (**Done**), which is a provenance link,
not a dependency. TKT-146 and TKT-165, named as related-in-kind in the description, are Backlog and
are neither blockers nor in scope.

**Status verified against the board before entering, not taken from the request:** `status: Ready`,
`labels: []`, `readiness` fully populated with no `open` item. Entering at step 3 (claim) is therefore
correct rather than a skipped shaping.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.** Stated explicitly rather than left silent. The work adds a
recovery mechanism on the **refund** path; even though ADR-038 §7 and the ticket both scope it to the
already-durable reversal obligations and explicitly *not* to the money leg, the ticket's own quality
gate reads *"money untouched"* — a claim that has to be demonstrated, not assumed. Expected to touch a
service's startup wiring and plausibly a migration and/or deployment contract (the `ACCESS_URL`
readiness question is an explicit AC). Two of the label's four carve-outs are in play. The plan gate
stands.

**Branch:** `TKT-163-refund-reversal-reconciler` off `origin/main` @ `bf6c054a`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — `gpt-5.6-luna` (config.models.plan)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` via the codex companion**, effort high, read-only, against the real
tree at `origin/main` @ `bf6c054a`. Verified read-only after the run: `git status --short` was
empty, so no sandbox breach (the TKT-104 shape). Posted verbatim below, apart from the codex
session trailer.

The critique (`config.models.planReview: main-agent`) follows in the next comment; this is the
draft as received, unamended, so the delta is auditable.

---

# Approach

Add a dedicated `internal/reversal` runner for completed refunds whose `tickets_voided_at` or `capacity_returned_at` remains `NULL`.

The runner will:

1. Select outstanding, retryable refund rows with a joined `orders → reservations` read so `OrganizerID` and `HoldID` are populated. `LookupRefundByID` cannot be reused because it intentionally omits `HoldID` (`services/commerce/internal/store/refunds.go:242-256`), while `BindOrderRefund` shows the required join (`services/commerce/internal/store/refunds.go:106-136`).
2. Claim rows with a lease, claim token, `SKIP LOCKED`, next-attempt time, and attempt counter.
3. Drive each row sequentially through the existing `refunds.Service.DriveReversal`, preserving its ticket-before-capacity ordering (`services/commerce/internal/refunds/service.go:110-126`).
4. Requeue incomplete transient work with capped exponential backoff.
5. Exclude known permanently undischargeable partial seated refunds from repeated claims while exposing them through metrics and documentation. The reservation’s `seat_identities` presence is the seated marker (`services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/0013_reservation_seats.sql:22-25`), and inventory explicitly refuses partial seated returns (`services/inventory/internal/store/refund_returns.go:113-133`).
6. Add a database guard preventing `capacity_returned_at` from being recorded before `tickets_voided_at`.

This deliberately exercises the “adding one later” option rejected in ADR-038 §7 (`docs/adr/ADR-038-refund-reversal-ticket-voiding.md:138-146`). The requirement now exists, so the earlier cost argument no longer applies.

The new runner remains separate from both existing runners:

- It must not extend `internal/recovery`: checkout recovery has different eligibility and terminal-state semantics (`services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner.go:1-11`).
- It must not merge into `internal/bulkrefund`: its package explicitly rejects merging state machines (`services/commerce/internal/bulkrefund/runner.go:1-11`), and bulk refund only sees orders in cancellation books, not ordinary staff refunds (`services/commerce/internal/bulkrefund/runner.go:111-139`).
- An external cron or admin replay endpoint is rejected because it would still need durable claiming, backoff, fencing, and the same commerce database query, while making completion depend on another deployment component.
- An outbox/event-driven retry is rejected because the failure is a durable row obligation, not a missing event; access outages and issuance lag require revisiting existing rows.

ADR-040’s limitation remains true for the bulk runner, but does not apply to this dedicated reconciler: `DriveReversal` accepts the persisted `Refund` directly and does not require the original idempotency key (`services/commerce/internal/bulkrefund/runner.go:44-49`). Amend ADR-040 to clarify that its “reported, not repaired” rule is scoped to cancellation runs.

# Open decisions

- **`ACCESS_URL` readiness — Recommended: readiness failure, liveness preserved.** Split the currently shared handlers (`services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go:219-233`) so `/healthz` remains a DB/NATS liveness check while `/readyz` adds an `access_configured` check. The current shared handler would make a readiness failure also fail liveness (`shared/go/httpx/healthz.go:37-57`), so adding the check to the existing handler is rejected. The runner will not claim ticket-voiding work when the URL is absent, but will continue capacity-only work and emit outstanding metrics. Compose already supplies `ACCESS_URL` (`compose.yaml:238-244`).

  The most reversible option is to retain optional startup and use only metrics plus an alert. It is rejected because a deployment with no access URL would otherwise accept refunds while silently accumulating an obligation.

- **Retry policy — Recommended: unlimited transient retries with capped exponential backoff.** A permanent attempt limit would reintroduce the original “money moved, tickets still valid, no driver” failure after a sufficiently long outage. Use environment-tunable interval and batch defaults, with a maximum per-row delay.

- **Partial seated refunds — Recommended: leave the obligation outstanding and exclude it from automatic claims.** Do not stamp `capacity_returned_at`, invent a terminal success state, or repeatedly call inventory. Expose a gauge and oldest-age metric. TKT-164 can later make those rows repairable by adding ticket-to-seat identity.

- **Exchanges — Recommended: out of scope.** The ticket and COS name refunds, and the readiness note concerns the two refund obligations. Exchanges need a separate eligibility/read model and follow-up, referenced by the interrupted-exchange work as TKT-167 (`docs/reviews/2026-08-08-sdlc-board-validation.md:102`). The most reversible option is a shared polymorphic reconciler, but that would prematurely couple refund and exchange state machines.

# Definition of Done

- [ ] **COS 1:** In the composed stack, a refund created while Access is stopped is automatically revisited after Access restarts; both refund obligation timestamps become non-null without replaying the request. Permanently undischargeable partial seated rows remain visibly outstanding and are monitored.
- [ ] **COS 2:** Repeated claims, worker crashes, lease expiry, and duplicate runner instances converge on one access void, one inventory return, and stable timestamps; no money operation is added or retried.
- [ ] **COS 3:** A gateway smoke test stops Access, performs a refund, confirms the obligation remains outstanding, restarts Access, and confirms both obligations complete afterward.
- [ ] **COS 4:** ADR-038 explicitly records the reconciler and the new `ACCESS_URL` readiness decision; `/readyz` fails when `ACCESS_URL` is absent while `/healthz` remains usable.
- [ ] `make check` passes after regenerated artifacts, if any, are committed.
- [ ] Commerce contract and PostgreSQL smoke tests pass, including the new claim, lease, join, permanent-row, ordering-guard, and migration tests.
- [ ] Payments tables, payment facts, payment amounts, and payment calls are unchanged by the reconciler implementation.

# Files

New files:

- `services/commerce/internal/reversal/runner.go` — dedicated leased runner, retry/backoff policy, shutdown handling, and OTel metrics.
- `services/commerce/internal/reversal/dbstore.go` — PostgreSQL implementation of the runner’s store port.
- `services/commerce/internal/reversal/runner_test.go` — fake-port decision-table tests.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/reversal_smoke_test.go` — real-PostgreSQL tests for selection, joins, leases, fencing, backoff, and permanent seated exclusions.
- `smoke/refund_reversal_recovery_test.go` — composed-stack outage/restart demonstration using the existing Docker helpers (`smoke/smoke_test.go:344-350`).
- `services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/0021_refund_reversal_reconciliation.sql` — next migration after the verified current highest migration, `0020_reseller_credentials.sql:1`; adds claim/backoff columns and the refund capacity-after-void constraint.
- `docs/adr/ADR-062-refund-reversal-reconciliation.md` — durable runner, retry, monitoring, replica, and permanent-obligation decision.

Modified files:

- `services/commerce/internal/store/refunds.go` — add the joined outstanding-refund claim/read transitions and require `tickets_voided_at IS NOT NULL` in `MarkRefundCapacityReturned` (`services/commerce/internal/store/refunds.go:384-392`).
- `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go` — instantiate the runner through `srvHandler.Refunds()` (`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:146-159`), add interval/batch configuration, register OTel gauges, split liveness/readiness, and place shutdown before dependency workers.
- `compose.smoke.yaml` — set short reversal interval and batch values so the outage test is bounded.
- `docs/configuration.md` — document reversal runner settings and the `ACCESS_URL` readiness contract.
- `docs/development.md` — document operator-visible outstanding, permanently blocked, and retrying states.
- `docs/adr/ADR-038-refund-reversal-ticket-voiding.md` — amend §7 from “nothing retries on its own” to the TKT-163 reconciler decision and record the readiness change.
- `docs/adr/ADR-040-event-cancellation-bulk-refund-runs.md` — clarify that its non-repair rule remains a bulk-run limitation, not a system-wide prohibition.

No OpenAPI or generated-file changes are planned. There is no new HTTP operation; the existing refund operation and response already declare both reversal booleans (`services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml:378-390`, `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml:1047-1064`). Therefore `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` and frontend generated types remain unchanged.

# Test plan

## Test seam

- The runner’s decisions—claim, skip, requeue, backoff, shutdown release, and fencing—belong in `unit-with-fakes`, following the existing port pattern (`services/commerce/internal/bulkrefund/runner.go:26-49`).
- SQL eligibility, tenant scoping, `HoldID` population, claim leases, claim tokens, indexes, and the capacity-after-void guard belong in `store smoke` against PostgreSQL. A fake must not prove SQL predicates.
- The downstream outage and eventual completion belong in `gateway smoke`, because only the composed stack can stop and restart Access and observe the durable result.
- The existing `DriveReversal` call remains the sole reversal unit; it already enforces void-before-capacity (`services/commerce/internal/refunds/service.go:121-126`).

| Test | Tier | Invariant | What breaks it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TestRunnerRetriesAnIncompleteReversal` | unit-with-fakes | An incomplete reversal is revisited on a later eligible pass and a completed reversal is not revisited. | Finalizing the first incomplete result, omitting the second claim, or treating `TicketsVoided` as the only completion condition. |
| `TestRunnerBackoffPreventsSamePassSpin` | unit-with-fakes | A transiently failing row is attempted once per scheduled time, not repeatedly in one pass. | Releasing the row with `next_attempt_at = now()` or ignoring the backoff predicate. |
| `TestRunnerFencesLeaseReleaseByClaimID` | unit-with-fakes | A stale worker cannot clear or reschedule a row claimed by a successor. | Removing the claim-token condition from release or completion. |
| `TestRunnerReleasesUndrivenClaimsOnShutdown` | unit-with-fakes | Rows claimed but not driven during shutdown become immediately reclaimable and do not consume an attempt. | Reusing the cancelled context for release, or leaving undriven rows leased. |
| `TestClaimOutstandingRefundJoinsReservation` | store smoke | A selected refund carries the organizer and hold belonging to its reservation. | Reusing `LookupRefundByID`, removing the `orders → reservations` join, or omitting `reservations.hold_id`. |
| `TestClaimOutstandingRefundIsOrganizerScoped` | store smoke | A caller can claim only its organizer’s refunds. | Removing the organizer predicate from either `order_refunds` or `reservations`. |
| `TestClaimLeaseExcludesLiveRowsAndReclaimsExpiredRows` | store smoke | A live claim is invisible to another worker, while an expired claim is reclaimable. | Removing lease filtering, `SKIP LOCKED`, or expiry handling. |
| `TestCapacityMarkerRequiresTicketsVoided` | store smoke | Capacity cannot be recorded as returned while ticket voiding is still outstanding. | Removing `tickets_voided_at IS NOT NULL` from `MarkRefundCapacityReturned` or dropping the database constraint. |
| `TestPartialSeatedRefundIsVisibleButNotClaimable` | store smoke | A partial seated refund remains outstanding and monitored but is not repeatedly selected for impossible capacity work. | Removing the seated-shape predicate, treating a partial return as complete, or omitting it from the monitored count. |
| `TestFullSeatedRefundRemainsClaimable` | store smoke | A full seated refund is not mistaken for the permanent partial case. | Comparing only `seat_identities IS NOT NULL` without comparing refund quantity to reservation quantity. |
| `TestRefundReversalCompletesAfterAccessRestart` | gateway smoke | A refund made while Access is unavailable leaves both obligations open; after Access restarts, both timestamps become non-null without another refund request. | Removing runner wiring, selecting the wrong rows, failing to populate `HoldID`, failing to retry, or changing the worker ordering. |
| `TestRefundReversalDoesNotReturnCapacityBeforeVoid` | gateway smoke | While Access is stopped, inventory capacity remains unavailable even though the refund’s money leg has completed. | Removing the `DriveReversal` short-circuit, calling inventory independently, or removing the database ordering guard. |
| `TestMissingAccessURLFailsReadinessButNotLiveness` | gateway smoke or commerce API test | Missing `ACCESS_URL` produces a degraded readiness response while the liveness endpoint remains usable. | Mounting the same handler on both paths, omitting the access readiness check, or treating an absent URL as healthy. |

The outage test will stop the `access` Compose service, submit the existing internal refund operation, read the commerce row and inventory state, restart `access`, and poll the database until both timestamps are non-null. It will use the existing refund endpoint rather than adding a new documented 2xx operation, so the coverage gate remains unchanged.

# Risks / pre-mortem

- **Two commerce replicas double-drive a refund.** A lease scan without `SKIP LOCKED`, a lease shorter than the batch, or unfenced release lets two workers act concurrently. Use row leases, claim tokens, sequential batches, and a lease sized from the batch’s maximum two downstream calls. Access and inventory idempotency receipts remain the final convergence mechanism.
- **Capacity is returned before tickets are voided.** A second caller or future refactor bypasses `DriveReversal`. Keep both the application guard and the new SQL `CHECK`/`WHERE` guard; test the outage state before Access restarts.
- **A permanently partial seated return spins forever.** Inventory refuses it by design (`services/inventory/internal/store/refund_returns.go:130-133`). Exclude the known shape, leave the timestamp null, and expose a gauge/oldest-age metric. TKT-164 owns the eventual repair.
- **Inventory’s pool lock is overloaded.** Concurrent fan-out from every runner replica turns reconciliation into an on-sale contention source. Process claims sequentially per runner, keep all commerce transactions short, and perform the inventory HTTP call outside database locks. Inventory already takes the pool lock before the claim lock (`services/inventory/internal/store/refund_returns.go:52-81`).
- **The query never selects the rows that matter.** A query based only on `order_refunds` will omit `HoldID`; a query missing `status='completed'` will process pending money; a query using the wrong organizer column will cross tenants; a query filtering only `tickets_voided_at` will miss capacity-only obligations. Seed each mechanism independently and assert deletion of each seed makes the relevant test fail.
- **Missing `ACCESS_URL` leaves silent debt.** Readiness must fail, while liveness remains available for diagnostics. Metrics must distinguish missing configuration from a downstream outage.
- **A lease expires during a downstream call.** The successor may issue a duplicate HTTP request, but the downstream operations are idempotent. The old worker’s metadata write must be claim-token fenced; the design cannot fence an already-issued external request.
- **A successful test proves only the fake.** Keep runner decisions in fake-port tests and all SQL predicates in PostgreSQL smoke tests, following the existing split (`services/commerce/internal/bulkrefund/runner.go:26-31`).

# Out of scope

- **Money and payments:** no changes to `refundPayment`, payment facts, payment journal, or payment APIs; ADR-003’s compensating-entry rules remain untouched.
- **Exchanges:** no `order_exchanges` sweep; carry interrupted exchange reconciliation in TKT-167.
- **TKT-146:** no work is absorbed from that ticket because its scope is not documented in the repository at HEAD.
- **TKT-164:** no ticket-to-seat association is added; partial seated returns remain monitored but undischargeable.
- **TKT-165:** no inventory-side caller proof or authorization redesign; the reconciler continues using the existing internal inventory endpoint.
- **`bulkrefund`:** it continues to report obligations on refunds it did not create; this runner repairs them independently.
- **New HTTP operations:** no admin retry endpoint, report endpoint, or OpenAPI change.
- **Offline scanner revocation:** no change to the offline admission limitation recorded for TKT-162 in ADR-038.
